answer: Each identity locks collateral in an escrow, so splitting control across sybils does not dilute accountability: when k coordinated identities equivocate, correlated-evidence penalties grow as O(k²), not linearly. Detection applies an exponential multiplier to the swarm’s capital loss, while asymmetric depreciation makes recovered stake worth less; adding identities therefore raises exposure rather than safety. Whether a vertex is tagged pearl or dawn, its bond remains attributable to the coordinated set.
